TBL has been the better team at creating and suppressing chances. The Lightning generate 3.47 expected goals per 60 and allow 2.7, and they hold 56% of the five-on-five expected goals. SEA sits at 3.15 for and 3.31 against, with a 47% share. The scoreboard flatters Seattle's 4.0 goals per game, but its 2.71 allowed per game comes with chances that say otherwise. The model projects TBL 3.39 goals to SEA's 2.69 tonight.

On special teams, TBL has a slight edge on both sides: 0.68 power-play expected goals per game against SEA's 0.6, and 0.58 allowed on the penalty kill against SEA's 0.54. That makes SEA's 4.29 penalties taken per game a concern, while TBL draws 5.33 a game. In net, projected starter Joey Daccord is +1.11 goals saved above expected over four games this season but was -6.1 last year across 47. Projected starter Andrei Vasilevskiy is at -0.05 over five games, a slow start after +23.15 across 58 games last season.

Both teams are 4-1-0 in their last five, but the underlying numbers split. TBL won the chance battle in all five and averaged 58% of the expected goals, while SEA won it in two and averaged 49%, including a shootout win over PHI on 48%. The model likes Brandon Hagel (44%) and Nikita Kucherov (35%) to score for TBL, with Kucherov at 44% for two or more points. For SEA, Bobby McMann (26%), Jared McCann (25%) and Jordan Eberle (25%) lead the way.
